contract_plain_english: For a floating-point m-by-n matrix with m>=n, completed Gaussian elimination without underflow or overflow produces computed factors satisfying the exact backward equation L_hat U_hat=A+DeltaA and the componentwise bound |DeltaA|<=n*u*|L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2] In the square case the bound sharpens rowwise to diag((i-1)u)|L_hat||U_hat| and globally to (n-1)u|L_hat||U_hat|. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: equation (4.2)] The Doolittle proof preserves two distinct local coefficients, (k-1)u for row-k U updates and k*u for below-diagonal column-k L updates, and obtains the square result from k*u<=(i-1)u<=(n-1)u. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: equations (4.3a)-(4.3b) and final comparison] These are componentwise, O(u^2)-free bounds with no n*u<1 restriction. [PDF p. 4, printed p. 687; anchor: improved-bound discussion]

source_evidence.observation: For A in F^(m x n), m>=n, completed Gaussian elimination produces L_hat in F^(m x n) and U_hat in F^(n x n) with L_hat U_hat=A+DeltaA and |DeltaA|<=n u |L_hat||U_hat|; when m=n, the rowwise and global bounds sharpen to diag((i-1)u)|L_hat||U_hat| and (n-1)u|L_hat||U_hat|.

source_evidence.observation: The proof analyzes the mathematically equivalent Doolittle formulation, computing row k of U_hat and column k of L_hat from the displayed subtraction and subtraction-then-division expressions, with L_hat_kk set to 1.

The local residual for row-k U entries has coefficient (k-1)u, while the local residual for below-diagonal column-k L entries has coefficient k u, with the precise index ranges stated in the equations.

source_evidence.observation: The proof obtains the global n u bound from k<=n and, in the square case, uses k u<=(i-1)u<=(n-1)u for i>k to obtain the rowwise and global square bounds.
diag(f(i)) denotes the n x n diagonal matrix with diagonal entry f(i), with i implicitly ranging from 1 through n.
The improved LU bound is stated to hold for any dimension, radix, tie-breaking rule, and summation order, without quadratic terms, when underflow and overflow are absent.

statement.algorithm_linkage: The theorem is stated for Gaussian elimination generally. The proof analyzes the Doolittle schedule: at step k it computes row k of U_hat by subtraction updates, sets L_hat_kk=1, and computes the below-diagonal part of column k of L_hat by subtraction followed by division by U_hat_kk. The paper says this suffices because the formulations are mathematically equivalent, and the local estimates hold for any summation order. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Section 4.2 opening; PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Doolittle proof and equations (4.3)]
binders: m and n are matrix dimensions with m>=n, and A belongs to F^(m x n). [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 statement]
L_hat belongs to F^(m x n), U_hat belongs to F^(n x n), and both are the computed factors. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 statement]
For the local Doolittle estimates, k=1,...,n; equation (4.3a) has j=k,...,n, and equation (4.3b) has i=k+1,...,m. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]
conclusions: L_hat*U_hat = A+DeltaA exactly. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 displayed conclusion]
|DeltaA| <= n*u*|L_hat|*|U_hat| componentwise. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 displayed conclusion]
If m=n, |DeltaA| <= diag((i-1)u)*|L_hat|*|U_hat| <= (n-1)u*|L_hat|*|U_hat| componentwise. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: equation (4.2)]
For j=k,...,n, |a_kj-sum_{i=1}^{k} L_hat_ki U_hat_ij| <= (k-1)u*sum_{i=1}^{k}|L_hat_ki||U_hat_ij|. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: equation (4.3a)]
For i=k+1,...,m, |a_ik-sum_{j=1}^{k} L_hat_ij U_hat_jk| <= k*u*sum_{j=1}^{k}|L_hat_ij||U_hat_jk|. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: equation (4.3b)]
The proof derives the general matrix bound using k<=n and, when m=n, derives the sharper row bound using k*u<=(i-1)u<=(n-1)u. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: final coefficient comparison]
constants_and_indexing: The general theorem coefficient is n*u. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2]
For square A, row i has coefficient (i-1)u and the resulting uniform coefficient is (n-1)u. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: equation (4.2)]
The local row-k U residual uses (k-1)u, whereas the below-diagonal column-k L residual uses k*u. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]
The first row of the square rowwise bound has coefficient zero because i ranges from 1 to n. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 692; anchor: diag notation; PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: equation (4.2)]
definitions_and_conventions: Doolittle computes y_kj=a_kj-sum_{i=1}^{k-1}L_hat_ki U_hat_ij for j=k,...,n and y_ik=(a_ik-sum_{j=1}^{k-1}L_hat_ij U_hat_jk)/U_hat_kk for i=k+1,...,m. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: Doolittle update formulas]
U_hat_kk is the computed value of y_kk, U_hat_kj and L_hat_ik are the computed update values, and L_hat_kk is set to 1. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: paragraph preceding (4.3)]

diag((i-1)u) is left multiplication by a diagonal matrix and therefore gives a rowwise coefficient; its implicit square-case index range is i=1,...,n. [PDF p. 9, printed p. 692; anchor: diag notation; PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: equation (4.2)]

DeltaA is the exact backward perturbation L_hat U_hat-A; the displayed matrix product and local residual sums are mathematical products of already computed entries, not an additional rounded matrix multiplication. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 equality; PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: equations (4.3)]
error_notions: DeltaA is a componentwise backward error in the exact identity L_hat U_hat=A+DeltaA. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 conclusion]
Equations (4.3a)-(4.3b) are local absolute residual bounds for individual matrix entries. [PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: equations (4.3a)-(4.3b)]

The global majorant is formed from the ordinary matrix product of the entrywise absolute-value matrices |L_hat| and |U_hat|. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 and (4.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 694; anchor: derivation from (4.3)]
exceptional_values: Underflow and overflow are excluded. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 statement]

The only stated algorithmic success condition is that Gaussian elimination runs to completion; the theorem does not separately assume that A is nonsingular. [PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 statement]
Inputs and computed factors lie in the finite floating-point set F. [PDF p. 5, printed p. 688; anchor: definition of F; PDF p. 10, printed p. 693; anchor: Theorem 4.2 dimensions]
